title_ne: नवीकरणीय ऊर्जा तथा ऊर्जा दक्षता सम्बन्धी विधेयक, २०८३
summary:
The name of this bill is the "Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency Bill, 2083" (Section 1, Subsection 1, Page 7). The main purpose of this bill is to identify, promote, develop, and expand renewable energy to contribute to environmental protection, increase citizens' access to energy, and achieve sustainable development through energy efficiency, saving, and conservation (Preamble, Page 7). This Act shall come into force on the thirty-first day from the date of certification (Section 1, Subsection 2, Page 7).

The responsibility to identify, promote, develop, and expand renewable energy to increase citizens' access belongs to the Government of Nepal, provincial governments, and local levels (Section 3, Subsection 1, Page 8). The three levels of government must cooperate and coordinate with each other to provide energy access to citizens (Section 3, Subsection 2, Page 9). All three levels of government may take technical or other assistance from the Center to run projects or programs related to renewable energy, energy efficiency, and energy conservation (Section 3, Subsection 4, Page 9). To achieve energy efficiency and energy conservation, the Government of Nepal, provincial governments, and local levels must fulfill responsibilities and obligations to prepare and implement programs according to policies and standards, use and cause to use efficient technology and equipment when using energy, discourage unnecessary energy use, implement programs supporting proper energy use and management, prioritize and promote energy-efficient technology, equipment, and services, implement environmental protection and sustainable development measures in energy production, development, and use, and raise public awareness (Section 6, Subsection 1, Page 10).

Business establishments or sectors listed in the Schedule that consume energy in quantities determined by the Government of Nepal must fulfill designated obligations to achieve energy efficiency and energy conservation (Section 6, Subsection 2, Page 10). The business establishments or sectors listed in the Schedule include businesses, industries, factories, and commercial establishments, passenger and non-passenger transport vehicles, government, commercial, residential, and trade buildings, service sectors such as hospitals, schools, and universities, agriculture, irrigation, and drinking water sectors, energy production, supply, or consumption equipment, its production or import, and energy production, transmission, or distribution (Schedule, Page 27). Business establishments or sectors must fulfill obligations to prepare and implement annual targets, plans, and programs for energy efficiency and conservation, keep monthly records and logs of energy consumption, use energy-efficient technology and equipment, prepare and implement an annual action plan and targets to replace high energy-consuming technology and equipment, conduct energy audits, and implement recommendations of energy audit reports (Section 6, Subsection 2, Page 10-11). To execute these obligations, business establishments or sectors must arrange for an energy manager (Section 6, Subsection 3, Page 11). Operating business establishments or sectors must have an energy audit conducted by an energy auditor within three years for the first time after coming into operation, and every three years thereafter (Section 7, Subsection 1, Page 11). Business establishments or sectors operating at the time of commencement of this Act must have an energy audit conducted by an energy auditor for the first time within three years from the date of commencement of this Act (Section 7, Subsection 2, Page 11). Business establishments or sectors must participate in the energy saving scheme formulated by the Center (Section 9, Subsection 3, Page 12). A business establishment or sector that cannot achieve its energy saving target must purchase energy saving certificates from other business establishments or sectors that save energy beyond their target to complete the target, and if it fails to complete the target by purchasing certificates, it must pay compensation to the Center (Section 9, Subsections 6 and 7, Page 12-13).

To generate, transmit, or distribute electricity from renewable energy sources, the concerned person, institution, or body must obtain a license according to prevailing law (Section 5, Page 9). A person wishing to work as an energy auditor must obtain an energy auditor license from the Center, for which the person must have a Bachelor's degree or equivalent in engineering or energy-related subjects from a recognized university, at least two years of experience in the energy sector, and completed training conducted by the Center (Section 8, Subsections 1 and 2, Page 11). The Center shall grant an energy auditor license for five years by prescribing necessary conditions, and it must be renewed before expiry by paying the prescribed fee (Section 8, Subsections 3 and 4, Page 11). If not renewed within that period, it may be renewed within six months from the date of expiry by paying an additional prescribed fee (Section 8, Subsection 5, Page 12). The Government of Nepal may determine quality standards for technologies, appliances, or equipment related to renewable energy and energy efficiency by publishing a notice in the Nepal Gazette (Section 26, Page 20). Any person, institution, or body wishing to sell or distribute technologies, appliances, or equipment in Nepal must get them tested by the Center by paying the prescribed service fee (Section 27, Subsections 1 and 2, Pages 20-21). If testing shows excessive energy consumption, the Committee may recommend to the Government of Nepal to prohibit or ban its production, export, import, or sale, and on that basis, the Government of Nepal may prohibit or ban it (Section 28, Subsections 1 and 2, Page 21).
